output.title: Scope creep is a workflow boundary problem
output.body:
If you run a one-person business, scope creep is usually not a motivation problem. It is a workflow boundary problem: the work keeps expanding because nothing says where the task starts, where it stops, and what gets deferred.

The decision is practical. Pick one recurring task that keeps pulling you away from core work. It might be customer questions, invoice data entry, or lead follow-up. Ask two things: does it repeat often enough to describe the steps clearly, and does it have a measurable outcome? If the answer is no, automation is probably the wrong tool. If the answer is yes, a bounded automation may be worth more than another afternoon of manual work or the not-so-small matter of hiring.

For the owner who has tried ChatGPT but has not connected AI to a real workflow, the first step is not to build. It is to identify the one loop you repeat most often and check whether it is stable enough to automate without touching high-risk decisions. Human approval should stay in place for money movement and anything sensitive.

That is the core Bareni diagnostic: name one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and only then define a narrow pilot scope. If you want a simple self-check, ask: which task do I repeat most often that someone else could complete without changing the decision itself?
